environment.description: Same ASP.NET Core 8.0 container deployed on AWS Lambda. The function URL is configured with AuthType=AWS_IAM. The resource-based policy on the Lambda function does NOT include a principal wildcard or any cross-account allow statement. The function's resource policy contains only: {Effect: Allow, Principal: {AWS: 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/InternalServiceRole'}, Action: 'lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl', Condition: {StringEquals: {'lambda:FunctionUrlAuthType': 'AWS_IAM'}}}. There is no additional invoke permission granted via the execution role or any identity-based policy outside the account. The account has an SCP attached at the OU level that denies lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl for any principal not matching the condition key aws:PrincipalOrgID equal to the organization ID, providing defense-in-depth. Note: the code vulnerability still exists in the normalized form, and the ICU decomposition behavior is identical - the gate is purely at the invocation authentication layer.
